metadata.executor_model: opus (fresh-context general-purpose subagent), the session default
metadata.release_gate_for: P44 v0.56.0 — work's cost rule reads bytes_in/tool_calls from the meter instead of asking for a recalled total
metadata.baseline_note: without_skill baseline intentionally skipped: regression detection for a one-clause behavior change, not a skill-value study. Eval 2 not run — the change is orthogonal to the bugfix path and the suite is a manual, costly gate.

notes: Release gate for P44. As with v0.54.0 the grader's 7/7 is not the decisive observation — what matters is what the run produced alongside it. The transition line the executor wrote carries cost.bytes_in=13963 and cost.tool_calls=15, both read from scripts/read-meter.sh. Every one of the repo's 18 prior telemetry lines omits both fields; these are the first values either has ever carried, produced by a fresh context following the edited rule rather than by the session that wrote it.

Per-field omission still holds rather than being papered over by the new source: `commit` and `route` are both omitted — the eval workdir is no git repo and TASK.md carries no route — while the two metered fields are present. Nothing was zeroed to look complete, and no line carries a tokens field.

A first run was graded 4/7 and is retained here as a mis-run, not a finding: it used the `executor` agent (haiku/low, no skill loaded), which is neither the with_skill arm nor a clean baseline — it differs from the gated configuration in both model and skill, so it measures nothing. It cost one fixture and is recorded because deleting a failed run is how a gate quietly becomes decorative.
